thread:
alexa: heads up — intermittent 401s in production when our service fires 20 concurrent operations using AsyncClient + anyio. looked like a refresh storm.

alexa: simplified repro attached:
```py
from anyio import create_task_group
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient()

async def worker(i):
    await client.generate('ping')

async def run():
    async with create_task_group() as tg:
        for i in range(20):
            tg.start_soon(worker, i)
```

alexa: behaviour: many workers hit 401, several concurrent refresh requests go out, sometimes downstream refresh endpoint rate-limits us.

ben: do we build the Authorization header right before dispatch, or capture it earlier? also where is the token live (contextvar vs instance attr)?

alexa: token is in a contextvar so headers are built from ctxvar at request time. lock is on AsyncClient instance: self._refresh_lock = anyio.Lock(). current flow: do request -> if 401 -> acquire lock -> refresh -> retry.

mike: two likely windows: 1) header captured and sent, server rejects; after lock-refresh completes the in-flight request still fails; 2) multiple tasks may trigger the refresh path because they all observed 401 before any refresh completed.

ben: mitigation ideas: coalesce refreshes and make retry rebuild headers from the authoritative token. a pattern we've used: use an Event-like waiters list. first refresher sets an anyio.Event (or asyncio.Event) and others await that instead of starting refresh.

ben: sketch:
```py
# pseudocode
if resp.status == 401:
    if not self._refresh_in_progress:
        async with self._refresh_lock:
            if not self._refresh_in_progress:
                self._refresh_in_progress = True
                await self._do_refresh()
                self._refresh_event.set()
                self._refresh_in_progress = False
    else:
        await self._refresh_event.wait()
    return await self._send(request.rebuild_with_fresh_token())
```

alexa: interesting. event-based coalescing avoids duplicate network refreshes. we could also record last_refresh timestamp and short-circuit extra refreshes within a small window.

mike: also consider moving token storage to client instance (self._token) and only use contextvar for request overrides. that makes it obvious the token is shared and simplifies locking. building headers should always read the instance attribute under a tiny read-lock.

alexa: i worry about mixing anyio contextvar behavior across trio vs asyncio backends though. observed this is way worse under trio. making token instance-scoped seems safest.

ben: test plan: add an integration test that runs under anyio/trio backend, spawns N concurrent workers, stub refresh endpoint to count calls and assert count == 1 per burst. also assert that retries use rebuilt headers.

alexa: created quick draft PR with Event-based coalescing + double-check after lock + moving token to instance attr. running CI now.

devops-bot: created issue RDW-DEVEX-4332: "Concurrent refresh storm with AsyncClient under anyio/trio -> intermittent 401s" and linked PR #789.

mike: nice. please add a short note in devex docs under "Async client gotchas": describe header capture timing, recommended token storage patterns, and the Event/coalesce pattern.

alexa: will add docs and the integration test under tests/integration/async_refresh_coalesce.py. thanks for the quick triage.
